previous_last_sync.summary: Capoworks ECU now keeps fresh generic defaults valid when the firmware is built with a small cylinder fuel trim capacity. If the default firing order needs more cylinders than the compiled trim count, the generic MINIMAL_PINS defaults disable injection instead of leaving a configuration that fails validation. Explicitly selecting a larger engine preset is unchanged and still fails validation when the trim capacity is too small. The cylinder fuel trim documentation and the on-demand build guide are updated to describe this behavior and the build-time capacity requirement.

decisions.rationale: Fresh generic defaults are now made safe when the firmware is compiled with a cylinder fuel trim capacity smaller than the default firing order. On the MINIMAL_PINS preset, if injection is enabled and the firing order needs more cylinders than CYLINDER_FUEL_TRIM_COUNT, resetConfigurationExt now turns injection off, so the default configuration passes validation instead of faulting. This only affects builds with the cylinder fuel trim module and a low trim count; explicitly choosing a larger engine preset still enables injection and still fails validation when the capacity is too small. No tune migration is needed, but builders choosing a small cylinder_trim_count should expect injection to start disabled on generic defaults and must enable it only after selecting a preset that fits the capacity.
evidence: firmware/controllers/algo/engine_configuration.cpp: resetConfigurationExt adds a MODULE_CYLINDER_FUEL_TRIM guard that clears isInjectionEnabled for MINIMAL_PINS when getFiringOrderLength() > CYLINDER_FUEL_TRIM_COUNT
firmware/CHANGELOG.md: Fixed entry 'Fresh generic defaults now disable injection when the compiled cylinder fuel trim capacity is insufficient for the default firing order.'

last_sync.summary: Capoworks ECU fixes the Boost blend tables menu so the "Closed loop 1 adder" entry opens the first closed-loop blend table instead of the second. No tune values change and no migration is required; use the TunerStudio INI generated for the installed firmware and verify which blend table each menu entry opens before editing.

decisions.rationale: Capoworks ECU corrected the Boost blend tables menu: the "Closed loop 1 adder" entry now opens the first closed-loop blend table (boostClosedBlend1Table) instead of the second. Previously, selecting that menu item showed the wrong table, so edits could be made to the wrong blend. No tune values change and no migration is needed; regenerate or use the TunerStudio INI that matches the installed firmware, then verify which blend table each menu entry opens before editing.
